title: Issue Information
Global challenges, local responses: Exploring curriculum reform in South African engineering education
abstract: Abstract Background and Aim There have been significant higher education curriculum reform initiatives over the past 30 years across different global regions in response to a range of drivers such as employability, global citizenship, and sustainability. In professions such as engineering, a key focus has been on holistic graduate attribute development for scarce skills needs in increasingly complex socio‐technical sectors. This paper sets out to explore the drivers of engineering curriculum reform in higher education institutions (HEIs) in a Global South context. Design/Method Drawing on semi‐structured, recorded focus group interviews with 28 program coordinators and academics across 15 of the 16 HEIs offering engineering qualifications in South Africa, the research team set out to determine what kinds of curriculum reform initiatives were being undertaken, who was responsible for initiating, implementing, and supporting these initiatives, and what were perceived to be challenges and successes. The emergent drivers were framed in relation to curriculum responsiveness theory analyzed using an overarching “critical realist” framework with structure, culture, and agency dimensions t

title: Collaboration rules: A narrative comparison of engineering students and practicing engineers' collaboration experiences and beliefs using structuration theory
abstract: Abstract Background Collaboration—including coordination, communication, and teamwork—is crucial to engineering practice. However, engineering students are often perceived as lacking key collaboration skills at the time of graduation. Purpose We used structuration theory to explore how differences between students and practitioners' collaboration beliefs related to differences between academic and professional collaboration contexts. We sought to demonstrate that the perceived collaboration “skill gap” in engineering students can be explained by differences between academic and professional social systems. Methods We conducted interviews with 30 undergraduate engineering students and 28 practicing engineers, and from these interviews produced 98 discrete narratives of participants' collaboration experiences. We thematically analyzed these 98 collaboration narratives to identify student and practitioner collaboration beliefs. We further coded four narratives for organizational enablements and constraints to show how differences in student and practitioner collaboration beliefs related to differences in organizational collaboration “rules.” Findings Students described boosting produc

title: Exploring supports for belonging as predictors of student outcomes: Different roles of co‐curricular and extracurricular activities in engineering by students' year in college
abstract: Abstract Background Although most engineering colleges offer a variety of co‐curricular and extracurricular activities to enrich students' sense of belonging to the college, existing literature has not fully captured whether and how the various activities serve to support students' sense of belonging and predict student outcomes. Purpose We investigated how engineering students perceive diverse activities as supports for their sense of belonging, and how these perceptions predict their engineering motivation, persistence, and achievement depending on their year in college. Method Five thousand eleven first‐ to fourth‐year students from the College of Engineering of a four‐year, public university participated in a longitudinal, multicohort study. They reported their engineering‐related motivation, persistence, and perceptions about the extent to which four types of activities (i.e., university programs; college programs; co‐ops/internships and course teamwork; student organizations and research) contributed to their sense of belonging (i.e., served as supports for belonging). Multigroup structural equation modeling was conducted to examine the relations among supports for belonging

title: The role of learner trust in generative artificially intelligent learning environments
Transitioning into engineering education: Diverse pathways of military veterans
abstract: Abstract Background In the United States, there is increased demand to expand the engineering workforce. Many military veterans have received technical training that can be leveraged in engineering. Their pursuit of engineering degrees has great potential to expand and diversify the engineering workforce. Purpose This study examines the pathways of US military veterans from high school graduation through undergraduate engineering education and explores the resources they use to navigate their transition into engineering study. Methods Applying Schlossberg's transition model, this multimethod study uses semi‐structured interviews of 28 student veterans in engineering (SVEs) across four universities. Illustrative examples integrate thematic analyses of interview data and path analysis of key event timeline data. Results Path diagrams illustrate that SVEs embark on diverse pathways and engage in multiple transitions across high school graduation, military training, and undergraduate engineering education. Military experiences, especially engineering‐related work, and encouragement from military supervisors, other veterans, and family contribute to SVEs' pursuit of engineering degrees.

title: Exploring engagement narratives among self‐identified Hispanic women's experiences in engineering counterspaces
abstract: Abstract Background Diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts in higher education are increasingly recognizing the importance of understanding students' lived experience. More research is needed to deeply and contextually uncover voices, meanings, and stories that are enveloped within the complex realities of Hispanic women in engineering. Purpose While the Latiné/x/a/o, Hispanic women population is one of the fastest growing ethnic groups in the United States, they receive only 3% of engineering undergraduate degrees. This research explored how self‐identified Hispanic women experienced engagement outside of class. Design/Method This exploratory qualitative research employed narrative inquiry design using a paradigmatic analysis method. We conducted two in‐depth interviews with five undergraduate engineering students who self‐identified as international Hispanic women. Findings By examining the narratives through a novel synthesis of a socio‐ecological framework of engagement and community cultural wealth, we identified three themes that tell the story of students' experiences outside of class: (i) Perceived benefits and level of involvement informed student dispositions and aspira

title: Parental Support for Chinese Young Students' EFL Learning: A Perspective of Socio‐Economic Status
abstract: ABSTRACT Previous research has examined the link between parental support and their children's learning achievement, but knowledge of how parental support is influenced by their socio‐economic status (SES) is limited. Using an open‐ended questionnaire and semi‐structured interview, this study investigated primary school students' perceptions of parental support for their English as a foreign language (EFL) learning in a Chinese context and then examined the data from the perspective of SES. The participants were 20 primary six school students selected from two primary schools located in distinctly different SES areas within a city. They completed the questionnaire and interview regarding parental support for their EFL learning. The findings show that high‐SES and low‐SES parents exhibited different support practices for their children's English learning in four aspects: parental monitoring, offering academic assistance, providing affective support, and supplying material support. A deep analysis of the data reveals that these disparities could be associated with four factors in parents' SES: educational level, profession, financial resources, and beliefs about English education.

title: Humanising Web‐Based Learning for Academically Transitioning Students Through Their Voices
abstract: ABSTRACT Web‐based learning (WBL) has been widely used to support students' learning and has demonstrated its role in boosting students' academic success. Little research has focused on strategies that students can use to humanise this mode of learning, especially academically transitioning students. To fill this gap, this study explores the pedagogical use of student voice to humanise WBL during students' academic transition. Informed by a qualitative case study approach, the study involved a group of female students ( N = 12) from a university in China who were academically transitioning to content‐based English reading learning while participating in WBL for out‐of‐class learning. During their semester‐long learning, data were collected naturalistically, including student‐instructor dialogues as well as the students' written reflections and interviews with the students as ways of eliciting their voices. No additional interventions were made. By mainly employing inductive thematic analysis of data sources, the study shows that over time, voice‐making seemed to empower students to agentively participate in learning, reflect upon their learning, and offer critical insights into the

title: ‘Strong in Will but Weak in Power’: University Teachers' Perceived Values and Pedagogical Approaches to Values Education
abstract: ABSTRACT This qualitative study investigated university teachers' value perceptions and pedagogical approaches to values education. Drawing on semi‐structured interviews, classroom observations and document analysis with 10 Chinese university teachers, the study identified five main value types emphasised by the participants (i.e., benevolence, security, tradition, conformity and self‐direction values) and three approaches adopted in values education (i.e., traditional, constructivist and critical approaches). The findings show that university teachers actively incorporated curricular values into their teaching and enacted these values through their own interpretations and pedagogical decisions. However, their practices displayed an imbalanced pedagogical pattern, characterised by relatively extensive content knowledge but less developed pedagogical content knowledge related to values education. These findings further highlight teachers' struggling agency in a standardised accountability context, where insufficient professional support constrained their capacity to enact values education in pedagogically meaningful ways. The study offers implications for values education reform and

title: Researching Children's Literature Otherwise to Decolonise Childhoods in Experimental Curriculum
abstract: ABSTRACT This article explores children's literature as a tool for decolonising childhood and curriculum through experimental reading practices. Based on post‐qualitative enquiry, and grounded in decolonial, feminist, and posthumanist theories, the study analyses two reading encounters with children using picturebooks from Global South. These experiences gave rise to assemblages in which children's agency emerged through relationality and entanglements with books, bodies, materialities, and spaces. We argue that literature and childhood, which is often subject to adult norms, can facilitate plural and situated readings that affirm children's worldviews and knowledge. This approach interrogates the conventional and universalist conceptualisations of childhood and reveals possibilities for reimagining the experimental curriculum as a relational and co‐creative space. The article promotes an epistemic and ethical reconstruction of research with children that decentres adult frameworks and expand new possibilities for children's subjectivities and knowledges.

title: Developmental Model of Academic Resilience: A Mixed‐Methods Study
abstract: ABSTRACT The purpose of the study is to holistically identify the protective factors that contribute to students' academic resilience and examine the mediating role of protective factors between school burnout and school attachment using an exploratory sequential mixed‐methods design, one of the mixed‐methods research designs. A phenomenological research method was used to reveal the protective factors of students who were able to show academic resilience despite various negative life events. Results show that the factors contributing to academic resilience are categorized as the subthemes of individual, family, school and environmental resources. The mediating role of academic resilience resources in the relationship between school burnout and school attachment was examined using a structural equation model. The results show that resilience resources play a mediating role between school burnout and school attachment.

title: The Evolution of China–Africa Higher Education Cooperation: An Integrative Review for Promising Future Directions
abstract: ABSTRACT Over the past 20 years, the cooperation between China and Africa in higher education has shifted from mainly providing scholarships to a broader partnership model. This model encompasses academic mobility, institutional collaboration, research networks, vocational education and digital transformation. Despite the rapid growth and increasing importance of these initiatives, understanding how they work, their impact on institutions, their sustainability implications, and their long‐term potential remains limited. This review brings together 39 pieces of evidence from English and Chinese academic literature, policy papers, institutional reports and collaborative frameworks. It critically looks at how higher education cooperation has developed under the Forum on China–Africa Cooperation (FOCAC) from 2006 to the most recent 2024 framework. The review explores four connected areas: the growth and variety of FOCAC‐driven higher education initiatives, their effects on African higher education systems, the challenges to their sustainability, and ways for future cooperation. The review argues that the future success of China–Africa higher education cooperation depends on moving from

title: Family SES , Shadow Education and Education‐Related Worry in Suzhou, China: Tutoring and Parental Involvement as Linked Mediators
abstract: ABSTRACT Parental educational anxiety is increasingly visible in competitive education systems, but less is known about how family resources may be linked to both lower and higher worry. Using a 2020 parent survey from Suzhou, China ( N = 91,967), this study examines how family socioeconomic status (SES) is associated with parents' education‐related worry through extracurricular tutoring intensity and parental involvement. Educational anxiety is measured as a 10‐item parent‐reported worry scale, not as clinical anxiety. Serial mediation analyses show an inconsistent pattern: SES had negative total and direct associations with educational anxiety, but was positively associated with tutoring intensity and parental involvement, both of which were positively associated with anxiety. Positive indirect pathways through tutoring, involvement, and their sequence partly offset the negative direct association. Although the serial indirect effect was small, it was consistent across robustness checks. The findings show the emotional ambivalence of family advantage in shadow education.

title: Embedding, Copilot, or Agent? L2 Teachers Modes of Collaboration With Generative AI in Providing Feedback on Writing Assignments: Rubric Influences, Workload Dynamics, and Barriers to Integration
abstract: ABSTRACT Drawing from the established human‐AI collaboration framework (Mosqueira‐Rey et al., 2023), this study investigated how L2 teachers at a research‐intensive university collaborated with Generative AI chatbots to provide feedback on tertiary‐level written assignments over 9 weeks. Data from thirteen teachers included 278 interactions with GenAI, 876 feedback instances, and reflective accounts of their experiences. Findings revealed three Teacher‐GenAI collaboration modes— embedding (human‐led), copilot (interactive), and agent (GenAI‐led)—with a MANOVA indicating that rubric dimensions significantly influenced their frequency of use. Post hoc comparisons indicated that teachers used the agent and copilot modes more frequently in the “language use” dimension. Conversely, the embedding mode was used most frequently in the “content” and “overall evaluation” dimensions. Although the a gent mode reduced teachers' workload in providing feedback on mistakes at the micro level, the embedding mode demanded more effort from teachers to give feedback at the macro level of students' assignments. Guided by Ertmer's framework (1999) on the barriers to educational technology integration, w

title: Pulling the Lever Without Moving the Machine: English Teacher Education and the Limits of Sexuality Education Reform
abstract: ABSTRACT In this paper we draw on complex adaptive systems ( CAS ) theory to explore how changing systems of teacher education constrain attempts to introduce expanded sexuality education curricula. We report findings from a mixed methods study of teacher educators' perceptions of their provision in relation to England's statutory Relationships, Sex and Health Education ( RSHE ) curriculum. Despite its statutory status, RSHE remains unevenly and inconsistently embedded across initial teacher education programmes. We argue that sexuality education reform is unlikely to succeed without matched, sustained investment in teacher education—and that without this, statutory curricula risk generating new negative feedback loops rather than lasting change. We discuss implications for how policymakers might design more systemically coherent approaches to sexuality education reform.

title: From Environment to Engagement: Innovative Insights Into AI ‐Mediated Language Learning Through Psychological Mechanisms
abstract: ABSTRACT AI is increasingly used in language learning, yet the psychological mechanisms underlying student engagement remain insufficiently understood. This study investigates the associations among teacher enthusiasm, learner growth mindset, and student engagement in AI‐mediated language learning, with a focus on the mediating roles of willingness to communicate, resilience and creative self‐efficacy. A total of 699 university students participated in a cross‐sectional survey, and the data were analysed using structural equation modelling and psychological network analysis to examine indirect pathways and networked associations among environmental, cognitive and psychological factors. The results indicate that higher levels of teacher enthusiasm and stronger growth mindset are positively associated with psychological variables, which in turn are linked to higher engagement. Network analysis further reveals that willingness to communicate, resilience and creative self‐efficacy are interconnected, with engagement occupying a central position within the network. These findings highlight the importance of considering multiple psychological mechanisms when exploring engagement in digit

title: The Effects of AI‐Powered Genre‐Based Writing Instruction on Low‐Proficiency EFL Writers' Ideal L2 Writing Self, Writing Enjoyment and L2 Writing Performance: A Quasi‐Experimental Mixed‐Methods Study
abstract: ABSTRACT This mixed‐methods study examined the effects of DeepSeek‐powered genre‐based instruction (GBI) on argumentative writing performance, ideal L2 writing self, and writing enjoyment among 71 low‐proficiency EFL undergraduates. A quasi‐experimental design was employed, with an experimental group ( N = 32) receiving 6 weeks of AI‐powered GBI and a control group ( N = 39) receiving traditional instruction. Quantitative data included writing tests (holistic and CAF indices) and motivation questionnaires, while qualitative data came from semi‐structured interviews. The experimental group significantly outperformed the control group in holistic writing scores ( F = 45.38, p p

title: Immersive Learning in Business Education: The Impact of Metaverse Technology
abstract: ABSTRACT Metaverse technology, supported by advances in Virtual Reality, Augmented Reality, Mixed Reality and Extended Reality, offers new possibilities for immersive business education. However, existing research remains fragmented across individual technologies, educational contexts and learning outcomes, providing limited explanation of how the distinctive affordances of the Metaverse can be translated into theoretically grounded instructional design for business education. Through a structured review of the literature and theoretical analysis, this study examines how Metaverse‐based environments can support student engagement, practical skill development, business decision‐making and cross‐cultural collaboration. It integrates Constructivist Learning Theory, Experiential Learning Theory and Cognitive Load Theory to explain how learners construct knowledge through immersive participation, develop capabilities through experience and reflection, and avoid cognitive overload in complex virtual environments. The study also identifies major implementation challenges, including technological costs, hardware accessibility, privacy and security risks, educator readiness, and cross‐cultu

title: Chinese Doctoral Students' Boundary Crossing and Integration Into Communities of Practice in Hong Kong
abstract: ABSTRACT Research publications have emerged as the key marker of productivity determining one's survival in academia. The pressure to publish is no longer confined to faculty members but has extended to doctoral students. Despite a growing research interest in doctoral students' research writing experiences, there is a lack of scholarship investigating the complexities of the writing‐for‐publication process among those students who achieve publishing success during their studies. Informed by the dual concepts of boundary crossing and communities of practice and drawing on data from in‐depth interviews with four doctoral students and their supervisors, this study indicates that scholarly publishing is an intricate process encompassing the doctoral students' transition across linguistic, geographic, and emotional levels. This three‐tiered boundary crossing enabled the participants' socialization and integration into the academic research community. The paper concludes by providing valuable suggestions for doctoral students, supervisors, and university administrators.

title: Carving Out Professional Learning Paths and Challenges of Foreign Language Teacher Educators
abstract: ABSTRACT Although professional learning (PL) practices of teacher educators have received some attention, the PL challenges of foreign language teacher educators in diverse contexts are under‐researched. Thus, this qualitative study aims to delineate the PL challenges regarding career aspirations, professional roles and research motivations of 22 senior professors in English Language Education programs in Türkiye, a country characterized by frequent reforms in education and teacher recruitment systems. We gathered the PL trajectories and challenges of the participants via semi‐structured interviews. The findings revealed that while the participants were mostly driven by internal motivations in their career aspirations and research motivations, a heavy lecturing workload, large class sizes, abrupt changes in promotion criteria, and a lack of financial and institutional support complicated their PL paths. The findings point to a compelling need for more institutional support and research facilities that can be actioned by universities to stabilize PL within a more massified system.

title: Predicting Grade 7 Academic Skills: The Role of Self‐Regulated Learning Competencies of Grade 2 Students
abstract: ABSTRACT The article describes the model and standardized web‐based tool for assessing indicators of self‐regulated learning (SRL) from three areas—motivation, cognition, and metacognition. The aim of this exploratory study is to investigate which SRL indicators in Grade 2 predict students' academic skills in Grade 7. First, 401 Grade 2 students completed the SRL assessment. Of them, 321 students completed the Estonian language and 313 the math national test in Grade 7. All predictors were included simultaneously in the structural equation model. SRL indicators generally showed stronger associations with language than with math outcomes. Cognitive indicators, particularly attention, showed the most consistent predictive effects. The results are discussed in relation to students' developmental level and cognitive demands of different academic areas. Findings indicate that it is specifically important to support students' attention and thinking skills and create a classroom environment that fosters a growth mindset.

title: Instructional Design and Practice of an Interactive Animation Course for the Cultivation of Computational Thinking Ability With the Support of Flowcharts
abstract: ABSTRACT Computational thinking (CT) has received considerable attention as a key competency in education, yet effective approaches for developing CT remain limited. This quasi‐experimental study included 63 undergraduates to examine the effects of flowchart‐supported learning on CT. The experimental group received flowchart scaffolding and was split into high‐ and low‐scoring subgroups based on flowchart application scores, while the control group received conventional instruction. Results showed no significant between‐group differences in general CT after one semester, indicating that general CT is a relatively stable construct. Within the experimental group, however, students with high flowchart application scores exhibited significantly greater creativity and problem‐solving. Moreover, the experimental group performed significantly better on the individual comprehensive course project assessing practical CT. Findings suggest that although flowcharts did not improve self‐reported general CT in the short term, they significantly enhanced domain‐specific practical CT and, among proficient users, were associated with stronger domain‐specific cognitive CT abilities. title: Unveiling the Fluid Impact of Self‐Concept and Self‐Efficacy Upon English Achievement: A Perspective of the Island Ridge Curve
abstract: ABSTRACT Self‐concept and self‐efficacy have received much attention from second/foreign language (L2) researchers. However, very few studies have empirically deciphered their similarities and distinctions. Even fewer have investigated how their contributions to L2 achievement vary across L2 proficiency levels. The current study examined the commonality and specificity of self‐concept and self‐efficacy and their relative contributions to English achievement and their fluid effects on English achievement across different proficiency groups based on the Island Ridge Curve theory. A sample of 369 Chinese undergraduate students completed two questionnaires of self‐concept and self‐efficacy, and their English achievement was represented using College English Test Band Six scores. Bifactor structural equation modeling (SEM) revealed that the combined scale shared one commonality factor and two specific factors. Multi‐group bifactor SEM found that the general factor and specific self‐concept factor were positively related to English achievement and their respective effects fluctuated across English proficiency groups.

title: Teacher–Student Relationship and School Bonding in Primary School as Longitudinal Predictors of Students' Academic Achievement
abstract: ABSTRACT This study adopts a multi‐informant (students and teachers) approach to explore the prospective associations of the teacher–student relationship and students' school bonding with students' academic achievement in primary school. The analytical sample consisted of 1349 Swiss children (Grade 1: 48.8% female; M age = 7.45, SD = 0.38, range 6.06–8.93) and 250 teachers. 976 children were followed up 5 years later (Grade 6; M age = 12.63, SD = 0.37, range 11.31–14.01). Sex, parental migration background, parental formal education level and the baseline of academic achievement at age 7 were control variables. Positive teacher–student relationship predicted mathematics achievement later. Positive teacher–student relationship and school bonding predicted language achievement later but not consistently. The quality of primary education teacher–student relationship seems to play a crucial role in students' academic achievement. Educational and political implications are discussed.

title: The Road Ahead: Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Experiential Learning in Higher Education
abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial Intelligence (AI) presents promising opportunities to enhance experiential learning, but successful integration faces complex obstacles that require careful navigation. This systematic review followed the PRISMA guidelines to synthesise findings from 85 peer‐reviewed studies published in Scopus‐indexed journals on the application of AI technologies in experiential higher education across diverse domains. Results indicate that AI‐based tools such as intelligent tutoring systems, immersive simulations, and virtual reality environments can increase student engagement, motivation, self‐efficacy, and learning outcomes by providing interactive platforms aligned with experiential learning principles. However, findings also highlight significant challenges in effectively leveraging AI to complement rather than replace holistic, human‐centred educational experiences. Many current AI applications lack customisation for diverse learning styles and student backgrounds. Further research is critically needed on adaptive AI systems capable of providing personalised support tailored to individual learners' needs. Substantial teacher training and curriculum redesign are essentia

title: Exploring the Educational Linguistic Landscape Through Cultural Capital Theory: A Case Study of a Rural Primary School in China
abstract: ABSTRACT Research on linguistic landscapes in educational settings has highlighted their role in reflecting institutional ideologies and shaping school culture, yet little attention has been paid to rural schools, where signage may carry heightened symbolic significance. Grounded in Bourdieu's theory of cultural capital, this study aims to examine how cultural capital is represented and transmitted through a campus linguistic landscape of a rural primary school. Adopting a mixed‐methods design, the study collected data from a rural primary school, combining quantitative analysis of sign features with qualitative interpretation of students' perceptions. A total of 180 signs were collected, and interviews were conducted with 30 students to capture both visual patterns and lived experiences. Data were processed through content, discourse and thematic analyses. The findings reveal a predominantly monolingual and institutionally dominated landscape characterised by disciplinary and motivational functions. Five types of cultural capital emerged, namely institutionalised, educational, social normative, symbolic identity and participatory. Students demonstrated varied attitudes towards the

title: Examining the Role of Perceived Teacher Support on Left‐Behind Students' Well‐Being in China: The Mediation Role of Motivation and Resilience
abstract: ABSTRACT Since learners believe that their teachers can offer them chances to choose, support them in autonomous problem solving, and comprehend their internal feelings, teacher support results in the feeling of being loved and cared for. At the same time, the significance of motivation and resilience on the well‐being of left‐behind students (LBS) has been emphasized within the educational sphere. The present research investigated the way teacher support affects learners' well‐being, with internal motivation and educational resilience as mediators. A total of 258 LBS were surveyed in the present research. The results revealed that teacher support significantly predicted both resilience and motivation (explaining 26.4% and 46.6% of their variance, respectively). Both mediators, in turn, significantly predicted well‐being. The model explained 18.7% of the variance in well‐being. The study indicated the significance of teacher support to the LBS's well‐being; therefore, maintaining the theoretical importance for enhancing their motivation and resilience.

title: School Leadership Perspectives on Policies Related to Open Educational Resources in Primary and Secondary Education: Implications for Policy Development Through the Lens of UNESCO 's Recommendations
abstract: ABSTRACT To ensure inclusive and equitable quality education for all, high‐quality open educational resources (OER) are essential. However, the lack of appropriate policies governing the development and adoption of OER presents a barrier to their application in schools. Based on relevant UNESCO guidelines of OER, this study aims to inform policy development by leveraging insights from school leaders in Hong Kong. A territory‐wide survey of 102 school leaders, representing over 10% of Hong Kong schools, and follow‐up interviews with approximately 20% of the survey participants who volunteered to be interviewed ( n = 19) were conducted to investigate current school policies related to OER. Situated within schools' broader digital‐resource practices, the findings reveal areas requiring government intervention to address challenges, including resource accessibility, quality assurance, the need for teacher training, and the establishment of clear guidelines for resource adoption. In line with UNESCO's Building Blocks for OER policy development, this study provides insights into policy interventions that encompass (1) resource development and management strategies at both territorial and

title: The Role of Faith‐Based Organisations in ‘Secular’ International Development Education: Theorising Religions and Development With an Exploratory Case Study
abstract: ABSTRACT Faith‐based organisations (FBOs) are recognised by the development community as key organisations and partners in development cooperation. Yet commitments to secularism underlying international development cooperation in policy and practice have—to a certain extent—restricted theoretical and empirical study of the involvement and contribution of FBOs in development cooperation in general and development education in particular. With this paper, we aim to widen our conceptual approach to the role of religion in international development education by engaging a theory of non‐Western secularism. With this theoretical development, we analyse an exploratory case study of the Presentation congregation and its global advocacy mission, the International Presentation Association, as a space to consider the role of FBOs in international development education through the lens of non‐Western secularism.

title: The Effect of Nursing Students' Metaverse Perception on Flexible Thinking in Learning: A Path Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT It is expected that nursing students will demonstrate flexibility in their thinking as they learn, enabling them to solve problems, produce solutions, and establish cooperation. The development of flexible thinking can be facilitated by the use of the metaverse, which is a technological innovation and a three‐dimensional virtual world. This study aims to examine how nursing students' metaverse perception affects flexible thinking in learning and to investigate the relationship between them. This research has a descriptive and exploratory design. The study was conducted between October and November 2024 with the participation of 494 nursing students. Three instruments were employed for the collection of data in a face‐to‐face setting within the classroom environment. The instruments utilized in the study were the Descriptive Characteristics Form, the Metaverse Perception Scale for Nursing Students, and the Flexible Thinking in Learning Scale. The statistical analysis was conducted with a significance value of p β = 0.653, R = 0.590, p

title: School Climate, Teaching Enjoyment, Resilience and Work Engagement Among University Teachers in AI ‐Driven Higher Education: A Multi‐Group Structural Equation Modelling Study
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigated the relationships among school climate, teaching enjoyment, resilience and work engagement among university teachers, while further examining gender differences in these relationships. An explanatory sequential mixed‐methods design was adopted. In the quantitative phase, survey data were collected from 658 university teachers and analysed using structural equation modelling and multi‐group analysis. The quantitative data were processed using SPSS 27.0 and AMOS 26.0, while the qualitative interview data were analysed with MAXQDA 24 through thematic analysis. In the qualitative phase, semi‐structured interviews were conducted with 10 teachers to further explain the observed gender differences. The results showed that school climate was positively associated with teaching enjoyment, resilience and work engagement, while both teaching enjoyment and resilience were positively associated with work engagement. In addition, significant gender differences were found in two structural paths: the association between school climate and work engagement was stronger among male teachers, whereas the association between teaching enjoyment and work engagement was st

title: Artificial Intelligence in Education: A Dual Perspective From Academics and Students on Its Transformative Potential
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in higher education institutions in Kazakhstan. It aims to explore students' and academics' perceptions, usage patterns, challenges, and training needs. The findings show that AI is increasingly seen as a transformative academic tool, especially for research, language learning, writing support and problem‐solving. Although many participants first encountered AI through media exposure or academic requirements, their engagement has shifted from initial scepticism to routine use, with many reporting daily reliance on AI tools. Participants highlighted AI's potential to create more personalised and interactive learning environments, particularly through applications like chatbots and adaptive learning systems. However, concerns were raised about over‐dependence on AI, which could weaken critical thinking and problem‐solving skills. These concerns align with previous research warning of passive learning behaviours in AI‐supported educational settings. Despite widespread AI adoption, the study identifies significant gaps in institutional infrastructure and the absence of systematic training prog

title: The Interplay of Positive Reframing, Mindfulness, and Growth Mindset in Shaping Career Aspirations: A Mixed‐Methods Study
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the associations among positive reframing, mindfulness, growth mindset, and career aspirations in a sample of 308 undergraduate students from a public university in Eastern China. Using a convergent parallel mixed‐methods design, quantitative data were collected through validated self‐report scales, and qualitative data were gathered via semi‐structured interviews with a subset of 20 participants. Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) revealed significant direct and indirect pathways of positive reframing and mindfulness in relation to career aspirations, with growth mindset as a significant mediator in these relationships. The thematic analysis of the interview data provided deeper insights, illustrating how students leverage positive reframing and mindfulness to cultivate resilience, focus, and self‐awareness, which in turn are linked to a growth mindset and ambitious career goals. The integration of quantitative and qualitative findings underscores the pivotal role of a growth mindset as a foundation for career development and highlights the need for interventions that foster positive psychological traits in students. This study contributes to the

title: “Histogogy”: Trend and Thematic Analysis on Pedagogical History Education (1993–2024)
abstract: ABSTRACT In history education, pedagogy is essential, particularly for fostering students' understanding of history. The ongoing dearth of thorough and insightful research on research trends and hotspots demonstrates the goal of this study. This study focuses on a bibliometric examination of patterns in pedagogical history teaching goals. Using the WoS database, 600 research publications spanning 1993 to 2024 were examined. The data was exported to VOSviewer, Bibliometrix, and Microsoft Excel. The findings demonstrated that teacher preparation is the primary area of interest in research on virtual tours for learning, with significant publication activity in the United States, Brazil, and Spain. The “Journal of Curriculum Studies” was the most excellent and convincing source, and the University of Murcia was the pioneering organization. The four domains were identified using the thematic map, and new regions were found. The study's findings may help foster global collaboration, strengthen the link between history and education, improve educational design, and identify new areas of study for academics, instructors, and educational policymakers.

title: Beyond Administration: How School Governance Practices Foster Happiness and Belonging Among Primary Students
abstract: ABSTRACT Schools are not only instructional settings but also critical social environments in which students' emotional well‐being, sense of belonging, and agency are shaped. While previous research has emphasized the role of student voice in democratic schooling, limited empirical evidence exists on how governance‐oriented practices function in primary education through participatory interventions. This study investigates how governance‐based practices influence primary students' school happiness and sense of belonging through an action research approach. Conducted in a public primary school in Türkiye, the study involved 15 third‐ and fourth‐grade students and employed semi‐structured interviews before and after the implementation of participatory governance practices. Data were analysed using qualitative content analysis. The findings reveal that structured opportunities for representation and shared decision‐making enhance students' emotional well‐being, strengthen their sense of belonging, and foster greater engagement with school life. Students who perceived their voices as valued reported increased confidence, motivation, and psychological security, whereas limited participa

title: Transformations in Children's Play in Rural Areas: Teachers' and Parents' Perspectives
abstract: ABSTRACT Play for young children in rural areas is changing with social, cultural shifts and increased digitaltechnology use. This study explores changes in play among children aged 4–6 in three Gunungkidul villages, from parents' and ECE teachers' perspectives. Using a descriptive qualitative approach, data from 21 parents and six teachers were collected via online questionnaires and analysed thematically. The findings indicate that children's play has evolved into a hybrid play ecology in which physical, social, imaginative, traditional and digital play coexist across homes, schools and communities, rather than shifting linearly towards digital play. However, notable changes were observed in the context and proportion of play, including increased indoor and individual play, reduced spontaneous group play, a weakening of traditional play transmission and shorter durations of imaginative engagement. These shifts were associated with digital access, weakened peer ecosystems, parental safety concerns, changing family time structures, the use of devices as time‐filling and calming tools and post‐pandemic social habits. The study highlights the need for school–family collaboration and

title: Goals of Well‐Being in the Context of Finnish Comprehensive School Education
abstract: ABSTRACT One of the central aims of education and educational policies is to promote well‐being. Laws and norms oblige Finnish schools to formulate the goals for improving the well‐being of the entire school community in the documents guiding the school's operations. However, little is known about how the policy shows up in the school‐level goals related to well‐being, and how the ambiguous concept of well‐being has been understood. This article examines the well‐being discourses that emerged in the documents guiding the operations of Finnish comprehensive schools. We collected 379 school‐level documents from 20 municipalities and analysed the data using discourse analysis. As a result, four discourses were identified: the individual‐centred, competence‐related, collaboration‐related, and development‐supporting discourses. Our results indicated that well‐being at school is not an unambiguous or universal goal. Goals related to well‐being are often described at an abstract level. The trends in education policy affect the discourses that emerge and produce goals in the plans that partly follow the paradigms related to schools and society.

title: Before and After Remedial Classes: Students' Attitudes, Perceived Learning and Behavioural Intentions in Higher Education Accounting
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the role of remedial classes as a pedagogical intervention in higher education accounting. Specifically, it analyses how students' attitudes, perceived learning, continued‐use intention and word‐of‐mouth communication are shaped before and after participation in remedial classes. A quantitative pre‐ and post‐intervention design was adopted, with data collected from accounting students at two moments: before the implementation of the remedial classes and after their completion. The study used previously validated scales to measure reciprocal benefits, social influence, recognition, motivation, attitude, continued‐use intention, word‐of‐mouth and perceived learning. Structural equation modelling was used to test the relationships among the constructs at both time points. The descriptive results showed that students' evaluations became more moderate after the intervention, suggesting a shift from expectation‐based perceptions to experience‐based evaluations. The structural results revealed that reciprocal benefits, social influence, and recognition positively influenced students' attitudes both before and after the remedial classes. However, reciprocal ben

title: Exploring Teachers' Professional Identity Profiles in China: A Latent Profile Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examined the heterogeneity of professional identity among Chinese teachers and estimated the predictive effects of demographic and psychological factors on professional identity profiles based on the self‐determination theory (SDT). Data were collected from 404 teachers in mainland China and analysed using unconditional and conditional latent profile analyses. Three professional identity profiles were identified: engaged teachers, involved teachers and dedicated teachers. The results showed that two demographic covariates (i.e., teaching level of elementary school, teaching experience of 9 years or less) significantly predicted profile membership. Additionally, significant differences were observed among the profiles in terms of teachers' basic psychological needs of competence and relatedness, in line with SDT. This research contributed to a more comprehensive understanding of the mechanism underlying teacher professional identity development and guided effective practices in teacher education.

title: Meaningful Physical Education in Focus. A Scoping Review
abstract: ABSTRACT Meaningful Physical Education (MPE) is a student‐centred approach aimed at fostering sustained participation in active lifestyles, yet evidence is fragmented. This scoping review aimed to map existing MPE research in formal educational contexts and to identify methodological, contextual and pedagogical patterns informing future research and practice. Following a five‐stage methodological framework and PRISMA‐ScR, we searched ERIC, Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar for English/Spanish studies (2017–2025) explicitly referencing MPE in formal education. Of 237 records, 44 met inclusion criteria. Studies were concentrated in Canada and Ireland, with emerging contributions from Spain and other countries, and focused mainly on primary/secondary schooling and physical education teacher education. Qualitative self‐studies and case studies predominated, while quantitative and mixed‐methods designs are increasing. Reported benefits included higher student motivation, engagement, and enjoyment and enhanced teacher reflection; constraints included limited time, institutional support and curricular tensions. We propose an integrative account organized around three intersecting

title: Understanding Student Engagement in AI ‐Assisted Learning in Higher Education: The Roles of AI Support, Teacher Support and Flow
abstract: ABSTRACT With the increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education, this study examined how AI support, teacher support and flow are associated with student engagement in AI‐assisted learning in higher education. Drawing on Self‐Determination Theory, a cross‐sectional survey was conducted with 677 university students from multiple institutions who had prior experience using AI‐enabled tools for learning. Data were analysed using structural equation modelling with AMOS 26.0 to examine the hypothesised relationships among the study variables. The results showed that AI support and teacher support were both positively associated with student engagement. In addition, both forms of support were positively associated with flow and flow was positively associated with engagement. Mediation analyses further indicated that flow mediated the associations between AI support and engagement and between teacher support and engagement. These findings suggest that student engagement in AI‐assisted learning is linked not only to the availability of technological and interpersonal support, but also to the extent to which students experience learning as focused, absorbing and

title: Teacher Educators as Sustainability Change Agents: Identity, Agency, and Disciplinary Cultures in EFL and Social Sciences Programmes
abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainability education (SE) is increasingly recognized as a critical aspect of higher education and teacher education due to global environmental, social, and economic challenges. However, limited research has examined how teacher educators in developing countries, including Iran, conceptualize and implement sustainability in their teaching practices. This qualitative narrative study explored how Iranian English as a Foreign Language (EFL) and Social Science (SS) teacher educators interpret and enact sustainability through the Identity–Agency–Disciplinary (IAD) framework. Twenty semi‐structured interviews were conducted with teacher educators from four public universities in Iran, and thematic analysis was performed using NVivo software. Findings indicate a complex, recursive relationship between sustainability literacy and sustainability implementation. EFL teacher educators exhibited strong awareness of sustainable practices' outcomes but reported limited integration of sustainability into their professional identity, enacting only partial sustainable practices. Conversely, SS teacher educators demonstrated conceptual understanding of sustainability but experienced ide

title: Moment‐to‐Moment Dynamics of Foreign Language Enjoyment: An Idiodynamic Study of Conversational Topics Among Young Language Learners
abstract: ABSTRACT Foreign Language Enjoyment has received increasing attention in second language acquisition due to its role in fostering engagement and communication. Although previous research has often treated enjoyment as a relatively stable trait, perspectives informed by Complex Dynamic Systems Theory (CDST) suggest that emotions are dynamic, non‐ergodic, and fluctuate over time. Drawing on CDST, the present study adopts an idiographic approach to investigate second‐by‐second changes in foreign language enjoyment during conversational tasks. Six young language learners participated in recorded interactions on four different conversational topics, followed by idiodynamic self‐ratings and stimulated recall interviews to explain emotional fluctuations. The findings revealed nonlinear, individualized trajectories of enjoyment, highlighting substantial within‐person variability. Fluctuations were closely linked to topic familiarity and interest, idea availability, perceived task difficulty, and cognitive effort. Familiar and meaningful topics generally facilitated higher enjoyment, whereas unfamiliar or cognitively demanding topics led to declines; however, moderate challenge occasionally

title: Teachers' Perspectives on Integrating New Technologies in Education: Embracing Artificial Intelligence
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examined teachers’ use of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in language teaching, the perceived contributions of these technologies to language teaching and learning processes, and the extent to which AI technologies are integrated into language education practices. The research aimed to evaluate high school Turkish language teachers' views on Web 2.0 tools and artificial intelligence technologies. Our study used a qualitative research method with a semi‐structured interview approach. The sample group was determined using the maximum diversity sampling method. Fifty‐four high school Turkish language teachers from various disciplines participated voluntarily during the 2023‐2024 academic year. Data analysis was performed using content analysis, and teachers' statements were frequently cited to enhance the validity and reliability of the findings. The study revealed that digital technologies and artificial intelligence applications improve the efficiency and practicality of lessons. While participants acknowledged the significant impact of digital environments on social life, they also highlighted negative impacts, such as screen addiction and cyberbullyin

title: The Impact of Dance Activities on School Liking and Public Speaking Anxiety
abstract: ABSTRACT The aim of this study is to examine the impact of dance activities, designed to initially involve large group activities, then paired dances and finally individual performances in front of a group, on second‐grade students' school liking, school avoidance and public speaking anxiety. A total of 199 s‐grade students (109 in the experimental group and 90 in the control group) and their 15 teachers participated in the study. After assessing the students' levels of school liking, school avoidance and public speaking anxiety using pre‐tests, classroom teachers implemented two specifically designed dance activities each week over an 8‐week period. At the end of the 8 weeks, students were re‐evaluated using the same scales. The results revealed that students in the dance group exhibited significantly lower levels of school avoidance compared to the control group. Additionally, the self‐confidence of students in the dance group regarding public speaking showed a significant increase from pre‐test to post‐test compared to the control group.

title: Exploring the Relationship Between Personalization and Engagement in AI ‐Assisted English Learning: The Chain Mediating Roles of Perceived Autonomy and Learning Interest
abstract: ABSTRACT Guided by Self‐Determination Theory, this study proposed a serial mediation model to examine how AI personalization influences university students' AI learning engagement. Data from 390 university students using AI‐assisted English learning tools were analysed using structural equation modelling. The findings reveal that AI personalization is directly associated with engagement and indirectly influenced it via perceived autonomy and AI learning interest separately, as well as sequentially through both mediators. These findings elucidate the internal motivational logic of AI‐driven engagement, enriching theoretical research on autonomous motivation and psychological need satisfaction within intelligent language learning contexts. On a practical level, the current study offers evidence‐based suggestions for designing AI tools that support learning interest and sustained engagement in higher education.

title: Social, Motivational, and Methodological Pathways to Behavioural Engagement and Psychological Regulation in AI ‐Enhanced EFL Learning: The Roles of Self‐Efficacy and Perceived Fairness
abstract: ABSTRACT The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) education contexts has reshaped how learners interact, stay motivated and manage their learning experiences. However, limited empirical work has examined how social, motivational, and methodological factors operate together to explain learner engagement and emotional regulation in AI‐enhanced EFL education contexts. This study explored the relationships among social interaction quality, learner self‐efficacy, task motivation, perceived methodological fairness of AI‐supported assessment, behavioural engagement and psychological regulation. Survey data were collected from 497 Chinese undergraduate EFL learners who had prior experience with AI‐assisted English learning. Structural equation modelling (SEM) was conducted using AMOS version 24 to test both direct and indirect relationships among the study variables. The results showed that social interaction quality was positively related to self‐efficacy, task motivation and perceived methodological fairness. Self‐efficacy and task motivation emerged as strong predictors of behavioural engagement, while perceived methodological fairness playe

title: Large Language Models in Electrical and Computer Engineering Education: Opportunities, Challenges and the Road Ahead
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrical and Computer Engineering (EE/CE) education encompasses the rigorous study of electronic systems, computing architectures, embedded platforms, signal processing and hardware–software integration. Its inherently multidisciplinary nature demands mastery of mathematical modelling and experimental validation skills that pose substantial cognitive and logistical challenges to learners and instructors alike. The rapid emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) offers transformative potential for mitigating these challenges, yet their integration into EE/CE pedagogy remains underexplored. This paper delivers a domain‐specific analysis of LLM adoption in EE/CE education. We first classify pedagogical applications across teaching, learning, and course‐specific use cases by highlighting their role in programming, simulation, circuit design, IoT/embedded systems and capstone projects. We then identify measurable benefits, including accelerated skill acquisition and improved student autonomy, while rigorously examining risks such as academic integrity concerns and overreliance. Through structured evaluation, we reveal current research gaps, most notably the scarcity of empiri

title: Effects of Servant Leadership on Secondary Teachers' Well‐Being Through Basic Psychological Needs Satisfaction: A Longitudinal Study
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite growing interest in teacher well‐being, longitudinal evidence linking servant leadership to multidimensional well‐being through distinct psychological needs remains scarce. Grounded in Self‐Determination Theory (SDT), which identifies autonomy, competence, and relatedness as universal psychological needs for human flourishing, this study examines the mediating role of basic psychological needs satisfaction between servant leadership and three dimensions of teacher well‐being (workplace, life, and psychological). Using three‐wave longitudinal data from 719 secondary teachers across 28 schools in China, we employed structural equation modelling to test the hypothesised model. Results showed that servant leadership positively predicted all three well‐being dimensions. Autonomy, competence, and relatedness satisfaction partially mediated the effects on workplace and psychological well‐being. In contrast, for life well‐being, only autonomy and relatedness satisfaction functioned as full mediators, whereas competence satisfaction did not. These findings highlight domain‐specific pathways through which servant leadership enhances teacher well‐being and underscore the impo

title: Sexuality Education in Swedish School‐Age Educare: Teaching and Approaches in Informal Spatialities
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the somewhat underexplored field of sexuality education in Swedish school‐age educare and is part of a larger practice‐based research project on sexuality education in primary school. This paper aims to identify how and where sexuality education in school‐age educare could be enacted, and what it might include. Empirical data consist of example stories from the everyday work life of a school‐age educare teacher that have been analysed using the work of Annemarie Mol, John Law and others on complexities, multiplicities and spatialities. The findings show that sexuality education is conducted in informal spatialities such as the boys' locker room and on the football field. It also seems to be in need of approaches that include staff de‐dramatising, listening‐in and alternating between planned and spontaneous activities linked to sexuality education. Consequently, the study contributes a hitherto underexplored perspective by identifying and visualising sexuality education in school‐age educare.

title: Spanish‐Speaking Secondary Students Reading and Spelling in English as a Foreign Language
abstract: ABSTRACT Proficiency in English reading and spelling is essential, as many professional environments require both spoken and written skills. Literacy development in English as a foreign language poses challenges for learners whose first language is transparent, such as Spanish, due to the complexity and inconsistency of English orthography. Spanish‐speaking students often struggle with these inconsistencies, adversely affecting their reading and spelling abilities. While prior research has primarily focused on primary students, this study investigates the reading and spelling processes of 78 Spanish‐speaking secondary school students, aiming to highlight their lexical processing, sensitivity to rime consistency, and the relationship between reading and spelling performance. Participants completed reading‐aloud and spelling‐to‐dictation tasks using English monosyllabic words with different values of lexical frequency and rime consistency. The analysis revealed that reading accuracy improved with grade level and higher feedforward rime consistency. Although reading speed did not show significant differences across grades, reading latencies were shorter for high‐frequency and high‐rim

title: A Scoping Review of Research on Teachers' Mindsets in English Language Teaching Contexts
abstract: ABSTRACT Mindset research has contributed to a growing body of literature in English language education, especially research on teachers' mindsets in recent years. Despite this, a comprehensive view to advance this line of research is lacking. This scoping review aims to map past research on teachers' mindsets in English language teaching contexts, identify gaps, and provide future research directions. Following PRISMA guidelines, a search query was applied to Scopus, WoS, ProQuest, and ERIC, yielding 1001 records published between 2006 and 2025. Following the inclusion and exclusion criteria, 41 eligible studies were selected for analysis. Data charting forms and extraction were jointly constructed and discussed by the reviewers. Results indicated an increase in studies from 2022 to 2025, and different approaches were used to study teachers' mindsets. Within Dweck's mindset conceptualization, the studies, however, varied in their domain focus. Several themes were identified, including the influence of teachers' mindsets on their practices, identities, emotions, professional development, and students' motivational outcomes, and their association with subjects and background factors

title: Intersectionality as Curricular Infrastructure in Language Teacher Education
abstract: ABSTRACT The aim of this conceptual‐reflective article is to discuss how we could (re)imagine language teacher education (LTE) for challenging contexts by adopting social justice as a philosophy of education and the notion of intersectionality as a framework to inform LTE. The article first conceptualises social justice as a philosophy and then proceeds to make a distinction between social justice LTE and social justice in LTE. This conceptualisation reviews the recent literature at the seams of social justice and LTE. Second, the article offers a discussion of intersectionality, followed by how this concept has gained traction in LTE across different contexts. Drawing from the sections on social justice and intersectionality, the article puts forward guidance for an intersectionality‐driven LTE curriculum with the aim of preparing language teachers for challenging contexts. This section includes the proposed guidance, with special attention to ways of knowing, the practicum element of a curriculum, and assessment. In this section, readers will find acknowledgment of opportunities and potential tensions.

title: Reimagining UK Universities for Society 5.0 and Industry 5.0: Human‐Centric Innovation Across the Green–Digital Transition
abstract: ABSTRACT The UK higher education sector faces overlapping pressures from decarbonisation, digital transformation and rising demands for public value. Yet universities often address these pressures through fragmented agendas, treating sustainability, digitalisation and societal engagement as separate domains of action. This paper develops a UK‐oriented account of ‘University 5.0’ by reframing it not as a technological stage model, but as a problem of governance and capability alignment under green–digital transition. Drawing on publicly available system documents, including REF 2021, the knowledge exchange framework (KEF) and higher education innovation funding (HEIF), the paper adopts a conceptual‐policy analysis supported by one institutional vignette. The analysis shows that the UK already possesses important instruments for advancing University 5.0: HEIF provides capacity for knowledge exchange, KEF makes external collaboration visible and REF gives formal status to impact and institutional environment. However, these instruments remain only partially aligned with the 5.0 standard of human‐centric and ecological value. They are stronger at evidencing activity, partnership and im

title: Logical Transformation of University Governance in a Risk Society: Evidence From High‐Risk Teaching and Research Settings
abstract: ABSTRACT Universities are often imagined as epistemic institutions oriented towards experimentation and openness, yet in high‐risk teaching and research settings they increasingly operate as risk organizations. Drawing on risk society theory, this study examines how governance rationalities are reshaped in high‐risk environments within a university in south‐eastern coastal China. Based on 22 semi‐structured interviews conducted across the governance chain, including principal investigators and course leaders, technicians and laboratory managers, EHS and safety staff, administrators, and laboratory users, the paper analyzes how manufactured uncertainty and accountability pressures are organized in everyday routines. The findings identify four interlinked mechanisms. First, competence is reformatted from tacit expertise into auditable evidence through training certification, SOP sign‐off, access authorization, and formal record‐keeping. Second, accountability is organized through ‘signature politics’, producing traceable responsibility chains that redistribute exposure while encouraging defensive compliance. Third, risk governance operates through temporal regimes—approval lead times

title: Do Digital Cognitive Skills Matter in Academic Well‐Being? Student Engagement and Digital Learning Satisfaction as Mediators
abstract: ABSTRACT Students' digital skills are essential for their academic well‐being. This study aims to develop a model that explains the complex association between digital cognitive skills and academic well‐being in online learning. Using the Conservation of Resources theoretical framework, our study tests a hypothesised serial mediation model in which student engagement and learning digital satisfaction mediate the relationship between digital cognitive skills and academic well‐being. The results of our research, conducted on 289 university students from India who learn online, reveal only an indirect association between digital cognitive skills and academic well‐being. In addition, the results highlight and support the role of student engagement and digital learning satisfaction as serial mediators. This study reveals that digital cognitive skills not only enhance engagement but also have a favourable impact on overall satisfaction with the learning process, leading to the academic well‐being of students in online learning. These findings underscore the importance of exploring the mechanisms through which students' digital cognitive skills are associated with educational outcomes.

title: Empowering Schools in Times of Crisis: A Systematic Review of Leadership Practices During and After the COVID ‐19 Pandemic
abstract: ABSTRACT This review synthesizes findings from 226 empirical studies on school leadership practices addressing various challenges during and after the COVID‐19 pandemic. Five major foci were identified through the thematic analysis. It is evident that school leaders, regardless of context, devote significant time and effort to urgent crisis responses, including facilitating student learning, allocating resources, empowering teachers, addressing school and community well‐being, and managing the recovery phase. The importance of collaborative and community‐based strategies, as well as the role of digital instructional leadership, is particularly emphasized in the findings. Nuances in leadership approaches and practices across contexts, such as prioritizing technological support in the developing world and emphasizing communication and collaboration in developed countries, are also explored. Overall, the review contributes to the school leadership theory and practice by offering evidence‐based insights from a comprehensive set of studies across various national and cultural contexts.

title: Research of the Impact of School Digitization Levels on Students' Academic Achievement—Moderating Effects of School Type
abstract: ABSTRACT Digital transformation of education has become one of the focuses of attention and research in the field of education at home and abroad. This study aims to investigate the impact of school digitization level on academic achievement, to explore the deep relationship between schools, teachers, and students, to construct a theoretical model of the impact of school digitization level on academic achievement, to select school questionnaire data from the PISA dataset in 2022, to retain 12,734 valid samples after data screening and processing, and to carry out empirical analysis. The results show that school digitization level can directly affect academic achievement; school digitization level has a significant positive effect on academic achievement through learning behaviour; school digitization level does not indirectly affect academic achievement through teaching behaviour; but school digitization level can positively affect the educational effect through the chain mediation of teaching behaviour and learning behaviour. School type has a moderating effect on the chain mediating role of school digitization level affecting students' academic achievement, while school type also

title: The Changing Landscape of Supplementary Education in China: Historical Trajectories and Institutional Typologies
abstract: ABSTRACT Since the foundation of the People's Republic of China in 1949, supplementary education has been shaped by three very different paradigms. At the outset were Communist traditions in which China learned from the Soviet Union. Subsequently, these were mixed with, or perhaps subverted by, the market economy; and then the State reasserted itself. Each era had its archetypes, albeit with overlaps. First were forms of public outside‐school education institutions, including Palaces for Children and Youth on the Soviet model; second were commercial enterprises offering private supplementary tutoring facilitated by the neoliberal changes; and third were school‐based after‐school programmes established by the government to combat privately‐driven tutoring. Drawing on documentary research and on findings from the author's empirical research since 2010, this article analyses the complex patterns of supplementary education and its governance in China. It begins with a typology of supplementary education before turning to the historical eras. The comparisons over time and across systems expose dynamics that shaped the features of supplementary education in different eras. The article pr

title: ‘What's the Essence of This Profession?’ Spanish Teacher Educators' Post‐Pandemic Conceptualizations of Work, Pre‐Service Teachers and Emotions
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper reports on an interpretive phenomenological study that examined the lived experiences of teacher educators in Spain. Responding to a lack of research on teacher educators, the study sought to make sense of the participants' work in the current, post‐pandemic context. A framework that emphasized the dialectical relationship between agency and structures was used to interpret the participants' narratives. Three themes emerged to illustrate the essence of their work: wrestling with complex changes in students; responding to new technologies; and expanding their knowledge and instructional practices in teacher preparation. The participants also described a range of emotions that arose in response to these issues, which served as a thread across the themes. Implications and recommendations are discussed, including a stronger focus on well‐being for teacher educators and pre‐service teachers, additional professional learning opportunities and dedicated time and space for international and cross‐institutional work among teacher educators.

title: Design and Optimisation of Personalised Training Games for Special Education Based on Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
abstract: ABSTRACT Personalised training games have proven to be highly beneficial for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) due to the adaptive nature of the interventions in custom training games using reinforcement learning (RL). However, their wider applicability and implementation are hindered by issues such as low scalability, inability to adapt to real‐time changes, small training datasets and reliance on costly specialised equipment. A new framework to address these limitations is proposed using Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO), a recently developed RL approach that dynamically updates game interventions based on real‐time measurements of participants, such as behavioural measures and physiological signals. This approach shows significant improvements in performance, with an engagement prediction accuracy rate of 98% for E4AccData and Performance Data. Additionally, the involvement and performance of participants during intervention sessions show substantial increases, indicating that adaptive training games can effectively promote better learning outcomes for children with ASD. This study contributes to the field by proposing an evidence‐based intervention that can transfor

title: Reconfiguring Creativity: A Systematic Review of Empirical Research on Artificial Intelligence in the Fine Arts
abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reconfiguring the epistemic and creative boundaries of the fine arts, challenging long‐standing distinctions between human authorship and machine‐generated expression. Across artistic domains including visual arts, music and literature, AI is increasingly embedded not only in creative production but also in analytical interpretation, curatorial practice and immersive audience engagement. This systematic review synthesises empirical research examining the role and impact of AI within the fine arts, with particular attention to its implications for creativity, perception and artistic practice. A structured search of three major bibliographic databases yielded 723 records. Following rigorous screening procedures based on predefined inclusion criteria, 44 empirical studies were retained for analysis. The findings shed light on the emergence of AI as a co‐creative agent, destabilising conventional notions of authorship, originality and aesthetic value, signalling a broader cultural shift in how art is conceptualised and experienced. At the same time, the review highlights critical limitations, including the concentration of research withi

title: Cracking the Black Box of Non‐Cognitive Skills of Upper‐Secondary Vocational School Students: Empirical Evidence From Four Provinces in China
abstract: ABSTRACT Non‐cognitive skills are important for students' growth and future work and life. Using the 2018 PISA (B‐S‐Z‐J China) data, this study measured the non‐cognitive skills of upper‐secondary vocational school students relative to general high school students and studied the impact of family factors and school factors on the non‐cognitive skills of upper‐secondary vocational education students. The empirical results show that upper‐secondary vocational school students are not weaker than general high school students regarding conscientiousness, emotional stability or resilience. Parental emotional support, teachers' enthusiasm for teaching and school cooperation atmosphere have a positive impact on the non‐cognitive skills of upper‐secondary vocational education students. Building relational and emotional connections associated with people and soft resource inputs to enhance the non‐cognitive skills of upper‐secondary vocational education students should be the focus.

title: Navigating Bicultural Ecologies: Schooling and Life Chances in Roma Communities
abstract: ABSTRACT This longitudinal study examines 30 years in the lives of two segregated Roma communities in Hungary by tracing educational trajectories and adult life chances. It analyses acculturation processes, exploring how educational experiences intersect with bicultural home and community socialisation to shape the accumulation and transformation of forms of capital relevant to school continuity and attainment. Data were collected at four time points: at the beginning (1995) and end (2003) of primary schooling using adapted surveys, followed by biographical interviews with participants (2017) and interviews with local educational actors (2025). The findings illustrate the diversity of bicultural ecologies .
